solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spell "issue" in reverse

indicators.note: says the word for issue is read from its last letter back to its first

parts.note: to issue is to emit, send out

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to spell a word backwards, as in a spelling game.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell is a period, as in a spell abroad, so it means a stretch of time.

clue.text: For example, hurling up some limestone, magma, etc

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the run of letters is read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of limestone magma etc are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone is hurling bits of rock and volcanic lava upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Hurling is an Irish field sport played with sticks and a ball, not throwing; that is the trap the surface sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurling is played by sides of fifteen players, so it is an example of a sport played by sides.

clue.text: Old chairman has year in Irish county

indicators.note: the chairman has the year letter inside him, holding it

parts.note: Mao Zedong, the former Chinese leader, was known as Chairman Mao

explanation.surface: A former company chairman spends a year living in a county in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county on the west coast of Ireland, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Leaves office, concerned with omens?

parts.note: RE means about, concerning, as in a letter heading
omens are signs of what is to come

explanation.surface: A superstitious official quits after reading portents, wondering whether the job is doomed.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, which is what someone who leaves office does.

clue.text: Cloaked in scarlet, one's king is imperilled

indicators.note: the pieces are wrapped inside the colour as if inside a cloak

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
one is I, so one's is I'S
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king dressed in a scarlet cloak finds himself in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Something risked has been put in danger or exposed to loss, the same as being imperilled.

clue.text: Desert's peaks, bizarrely, for winter sportspeople

indicators.note: arranged bizarrely, the letters of desert's peaks are jumbled into an odd new order

explanation.surface: Strangely, the summits of desert dunes are used by athletes who normally compete in winter.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed skating is an Olympic winter event raced on ice, so its competitors are winter athletes.

clue.text: Ray eager to straighten out something ill-defined

indicators.note: to straighten out a mess means reorganising, so the letters of ray eager are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Ray is keen to sort out a vague, muddled situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is a matter not clearly covered by rules, where the boundaries are unclear.

clue.text: Fair request for assistance leads to nothing

indicators.note: the distress call comes first and leads on to the letter for nothing

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal asking for help
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A fair plea for help ends up achieving nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means middling, neither good nor bad, the sense of fair as in a fair performance.

clue.text: Chemistry equipment cook ruining cakes has sent briefly in

indicators.note: the cake ruiner has something, holding it within
with has, in says the shortened word goes inside the cake ruiner

parts.note: a cook who ruins buns by overcooking them is a bun burner

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of sent is dropped

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened by its last letter

explanation.surface: A clumsy cook spoils the cakes, and the sent message must be kept short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook ruining cakes' reads as a scene but is a whole phrase for one piece: a person who burns buns. 'Has' and 'in' work as one instruction, split by the other words.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bunsen burner is the gas burner used for heating in school chemistry laboratories.

clue.text: Meekly assures wretched refugees

indicators.note: in a wretched state, the letters of meekly assures are spoiled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone timidly reassures people who have fled their homes and are in a miserable state.
explanation.definitionFit: People seeking asylum have fled danger at home, so they are refugees asking for protection elsewhere.

clue.text: Understand bishop's responsibility

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... is to grasp, as in 'I ...'
second meaning: the diocese a bishop is in charge of

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to grasp an idea, and the noun is a bishop's diocese, the area under his authority.

clue.text: Chance to abandon golf for a leisurely walk

indicators.note: the letter for golf is made to abandon the word, so it is dropped

parts.note: to chance something is to gamble on it
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer gives up the game, taking a chance on a gentle stroll instead.
explanation.definitionFit: An amble is an unhurried stroll, a relaxed and slow way of walking.

clue.text: Great friendliness of bishop on one being invited into dwelling

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: the letter for one is invited into the dwelling, put inside it

parts.note: a home is a dwelling
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A bishop is invited into someone's house and shows great warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is cheerful good nature and geniality, from the French for good fellowship.

clue.text: Delegate's outside to help providing warrant

indicators.note: the outside of the word delegate is just its first and last letters

parts.note: to serve is to help or assist someone

explanation.surface: A delegate's external work in support of a cause earns some reward or recognition.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to merit it, and to warrant is to justify or merit, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Awful sights I witnessed, reportedly with son

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: I witnessed is I saw
S is the standard abbreviation for son, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone describes ugly scenes they saw firsthand, together with their son.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, 'I saw' is said the same as EYESORE, as the final R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is an ugly thing that spoils a view, so the plural means ugly scenes.

clue.text: In kitchen, no blender to raise

indicators.note: says the answer sits inside the run of letters kitchen no blender

explanation.surface: A cook in a kitchen without a blender struggles to make dough rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the nobility, elevating their rank.

clue.text: US inventor has no side, on reflection

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror reverses, so no side is read backwards

explanation.surface: An American inventor is described, after some thought, as having no side, meaning no airs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No side' is an old phrase for lacking airs, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American who developed the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: A month's broadcasts are astounding!

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: May is a month, so the month's is May's

explanation.surface: A month's worth of television programmes turns out to be surprisingly impressive.
explanation.definitionFit: To amaze is to astonish, so things that amaze are astounding the viewer.

clue.text: One finishes sentence? Party time!

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A prisoner completing a jail sentence celebrates with a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sentence' suggests prison time, but the definition means a grammatical sentence, which ends with a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A full stop is a small dot placed at the end of a written sentence.

clue.text: Left out of greeting that goes over saint's head?

indicators.note: the letter for left is taken out of the greeting

parts.note: hallo is a variant of hello, a greeting

explanation.surface: A greeting so subtle it is lost on a saint, going over his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes over his head' suggests not being understood; the question mark signals the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: In religious art a halo is the ring of light shown above the head of a holy figure.

clue.text: Possible German teetotaller getting in a couple of rounds

indicators.note: the abstainer gets in between the two rounds, placed inside them

parts.note: two Os, each round in shape
TT is the abbreviation for teetotal, one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A German who never drinks alcohol still buys a couple of rounds at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounds' suggests drinks bought, which suits a teetotaller joke; here they are the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name, so a person with that name may well be German.

clue.text: Terrible Tim trains road runner

indicators.note: terrible training scrambles the letters of Tim trains road into a new order

explanation.surface: A hopeless coach called Tim trains a runner who competes on roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Road runner' reads as a jogger or the cartoon bird, but 'runner' alone is the definition: someone who runs an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs an organisation manages it, so a runner in that sense is a manager.

clue.text: Five go astray, cutting round a French swamp

indicators.note: the pieces for five and go astray cut into the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: O is round in shape
un is the French for a
V is the Roman numeral for five
to err is to go astray, stray from the right path

explanation.surface: Five walkers lose their way and take a shortcut around a marsh in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun a place is to flood or overwhelm it, the same as to swamp it.

clue.text: Sleep is something easy to do!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sleep, especially roughly or in makeshift quarters

explanation.definitionFit: The verb is informal for bedding down for the night, and the British slang noun is a cushy, undemanding task.
